title: John Lewis unveils 20th Christmas ad, urging shoppers not to give up on gifting
title_zh: John Lewis 发布第20支圣诞广告，劝大家别放弃用心送礼

image.credit: Photo by Catarina Duarte on Unsplash
image.author: Catarina Duarte

lead: John Lewis has released its 2026 Christmas advert, a three-minute film titled Gloria and Pickles that marks the retailer's twentieth festive campaign. Its message: in an age of screens, thoughtful gifting still matters.
lead_zh: John Lewis 发布了2026年圣诞广告——三分钟的《Gloria and Pickles》，这也是这家百货公司的第20支圣诞广告。它想说的是：在屏幕时代，用心送礼依然重要。

paragraphs: The film follows Gloria, a grandmother preparing to welcome her grandchildren at Christmas. Hoping to delight them, she digs out toys from her own childhood, among them a pull-along dog named Pickles. The children, however, are unmoved. Gloria is on the verge of settling for cash gifts when Pickles urges her not to give up; she ends up building a 'secret den', where the family shares a festive memory together.

Everything used to furnish the den is, naturally, available at John Lewis. The closing caption reads 'Don't give up on giving', a nod to how readily younger generations are absorbed by phone screens, and to the enduring value of traditional, heartfelt gestures. The advert was made by Saatchi & Saatchi and directed by Lucy Forbes, with Kristin Scott Thomas as Gloria and Paul Whitehouse voicing Pickles.

As ever, the music comes with merchandise: Sam Fender's cover of the Rolling Stones' 'You Can't Always Get What You Want' is sold as a CD and a seven-inch vinyl at John Lewis, bundled with his 2020 cover of 'Winter Song', issued physically for the first time. All proceeds go to children's charities, an estimated minimum of £18,000. Mick Jagger, a self-declared Fender fan, said he was delighted by the cover.

The campaign is unabashedly commercial: nearly every item on screen, from Gloria's coat and gloves to the disco ball in the den, can be bought via a dedicated page on the retailer's website. Even Pickles is for sale, as Fisher-Price's Little Snoopy Pull-Along Toy, first launched in the 1960s and priced at £12.99.

This is John Lewis's twentieth Christmas television advert, the first having aired in 2007; its cultural weight dates from The Long Wait in 2011. Speculation that the retailer might abandon the format, given the expense, has so far come to nothing. Underpinning it all is a year-round push to lure shoppers back into stores — and a reminder that careful gift-giving may never go out of style.
paragraphs_zh: 广告讲述祖母 Gloria 在圣诞节前夕准备迎接孙辈的故事。她想让孩子们开心，翻出自己小时候的玩具，其中有一只叫 Pickles 的拖拉小狗。可孩子们并不买账。Gloria 差点就打算直接给压岁钱了，是 Pickles 鼓励她别放弃；最后她搭起一个“秘密基地”，一家人一起留下节日的共同回忆。
布置基地用的东西，自然都能在 John Lewis 买到。片尾字幕是“Don't give up on giving”（别放弃用心送礼），既点出年轻一代容易被手机屏幕吸走注意力，也道出传统而走心的表达方式自有其价值。广告由 Saatchi & Saatchi 制作，露西·福布斯执导，克里斯汀·斯科特·托马斯饰演 Gloria，保罗·怀特豪斯为 Pickles 配音。
照例，音乐也做成了衍生产品：Sam Fender 翻唱滚石乐队的《You Can't Always Get What You Want》，与他在2020年翻唱的《Winter Song》一起，以 CD 和七英寸黑胶两种形式在 John Lewis 发售，后者也是首次发行实体版。全部利润捐给儿童慈善机构，预计至少1.8万英镑。自称是 Fender 歌迷的米克·贾格尔表示，听到他翻唱自己的歌很高兴。
这波营销毫不掩饰带货目的：片中几乎所有产品都能通过官网专门页面下单，从 Gloria 的大衣、手套到基地里的迪斯科灯球。连主角 Pickles 都能买——它就是费雪（Fisher-Price）的 Little Snoopy Pull-Along Toy，上世纪60年代推出，定价12.99英镑。
这是 John Lewis 的第20支圣诞电视广告，第一支在2007年播出；它真正成为文化事件，大约始于2011年的《漫长等待》。外界多次传出它可能因成本高昂而停拍，但至今仍在继续。这一切的背后，是它全年吸引顾客重回门店的努力——也提醒人们，用心送礼也许永远不会过时。
